pages.title: Orbital Scan #0088
pages.text: $(bold)Subject: Residual Consciousness Capture$()$(br2)Post-mortem recovery of a Returned Architect has occasionally yielded a stable cryogenic core containing what ORSA legal refuses to call a soul. It is black, cold, and still thinks in straight lines.$(br2)Field note: the core only persists in approximately $(bold)50%$() of clean kills. The other half collapses into soot, static, and what one intern described as 'geometry flavored grief.'$(br2)$(italic)ORSA would like it on record that weaponizing the dead was not the original proposal. It was the second proposal. The first one exploded.$()

pages.title: Applications
pages.text: $(bold)Acquisition:$() Neutralized Returned Architects have a $(bold)50%$() chance to yield an $(item)Architect Soul$().$(br2)$(bold)Use:$() Reforge an $(item)Acheronite Blade$() with the soul, one $(item)Frozen Breath$(), and one $(item)Refined Acheronite$() to create a $(item)Soul-Harvest Blade$().$(br2)$(bold)Effect:$() The upgraded blade deals $(bold)+3 damage$() to documented Frozen Dawn hostiles: Frostbitten, Hollows, the Returned, Mimics, and other Architects.$(br2)$(italic)ORSA notes that if you're binding a frozen human will into a sword, you can at least spring for proper fittings.$()

pages.title: Soul-Harvest Blade
pages.text: Bind the Architect Soul into an Acheronite Blade, stabilize it with Frozen Breath, then pretend the extra Refined Acheronite is a moral sealant. ORSA assures you the screaming is mostly metaphorical.
